title: Curonian Lagoon: Svencelė & Nida Kite Week
subRegion: Curonian Lagoon and the Baltic coast, Klaipėda region

bestPeriod.window: **May to early October.** May-June and September have the strongest and most consistent wind; July-August is warmest with reliable afternoon thermals and the busiest water
bestPeriod.raw: **May to early October.** May-June and September have the strongest and most consistent wind; July-August is warmest with reliable afternoon thermals and the busiest water

accommodation.note: €60-140 per night, double, in Svencelė, Kintai or Nida; camp beds €30-50

transport.note: €120-200: flights to Palanga or Vilnius plus transfer, car hire €40-55 per day, Curonian Spit ferry and eco-fee

activities.note: Kite or wing gear rental €50-80 per day; lessons €60-90 per hour, a full beginner course €300-450

summary: A seven-day water sports & coastal trip itinerary in Curonian Lagoon and the Baltic coast, Klaipėda region, Lithuania.

itinerary.title: Arrive Klaipėda, transfer to Svencelė
itinerary.morning: Fly to Palanga (30 minutes from Klaipėda) or Vilnius and drive four hours. Klaipėda for supplies and a look at the old Memel warehouse quarter.
itinerary.afternoon: Transfer to **Svencelė**, a peninsula on the eastern shore of the Curonian Lagoon and the best flatwater kite spot in the Baltics: a huge shallow bay where you can stand across most of the riding area.
itinerary.evening: Rig check, kit hire, and a briefing on the local wind pattern.

itinerary.title: Svencelė: the flatwater week begins
itinerary.morning: Morning wind is often light; use it for a lesson, a foil session or SUP.
itinerary.afternoon: The thermal fills. Svencelė's combination of waist-deep water, a long fetch and a side-shore southwesterly is close to ideal for learning and for freestyle progression, flat water and a standing depth means falls have no consequences.
itinerary.evening: The camps here are social and international; evening barbecues are the norm.

itinerary.title: Kintai and the eastern shore
itinerary.morning: Kintai, further south, is a quieter bay with the same shallow-water character and fewer riders. Good for a long downwinder with a shuttle back.
itinerary.afternoon: Nearby is **Ventės Ragas**, one of Europe's oldest bird-ringing stations, a genuinely worthwhile hour off the water, especially in migration season.

itinerary.title: Cross to the spit: Nida and Preila
itinerary.morning: Ferry from Klaipėda to Smiltynė and drive down the **Curonian Spit** to Nida (about an hour, with the Neringa eco-fee for vehicles).
itinerary.afternoon: The lagoon side at Nida and Preila offers launches with the Parnidis dune as a backdrop. Note that the spit is a UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape and **launching is restricted to designated areas**, check locally before rigging anywhere new. `verify: true`
itinerary.evening: Nida's harbour: smoked fish, weather vanes, and the best evening light on the trip.

itinerary.title: Baltic side: waves and the open sea
itinerary.morning: Cross the spit to the open Baltic beach. In autumn, a northwesterly builds rideable wind swell here; in summer it is a 50 km beach for swimming, running and kayaking.
itinerary.afternoon: **Melnragė** and **Giruliai** north of Klaipėda are the accessible open-sea spots, with the Melnragė pier as the marker. Waves are short-period and messy compared to the North Sea, the Baltic is a small, shallow, non-tidal sea and it behaves like one.

itinerary.title: Big session day or downwinder
itinerary.morning: Whichever spot the forecast favours. With a car and both shores available, this coast rarely blanks between May and October.
itinerary.afternoon: A guided **lagoon downwinder** from Kintai toward Svencelė, or Preila to Nida on the spit side, with a support boat.
itinerary.evening: Last night. If it is late summer, watch for the **cyanobacteria advisories**, the shallow lagoon warms and blooms in hot still spells, and swimming is discouraged when a bloom is posted. `verify: true`

itinerary.title: Dawn session and departure
itinerary.afternoon: Palanga airport is an hour from Svencelė; Vilnius is four.

accommodationStrategy.name: Svencelė kite camps and cabins
accommodationStrategy.description: On-site accommodation at the spot: cabins, glamping tents and camp rooms, with gear storage, rinse facilities, a rescue boat and instructors on the water. €50-110. Being able to walk from bed to launch is the entire logic of a kite week and this is the only place on the lagoon that offers it properly.

accommodationStrategy.name: Kintai and Dreverna guesthouses
accommodationStrategy.description: Small village guesthouses on the eastern shore, quieter and cheaper, with easy access to the southern bays. Better if you want the lagoon's fishing-village character alongside the sport.

accommodationStrategy.name: Nida wooden guesthouses
accommodationStrategy.description: For the two nights on the Curonian Spit. More expensive and more beautiful, with the dune, the Baltic beach and the lagoon all within walking distance. See Trip 10 for the fuller version of Nida.

logistics.emergency: 112. Klaipėda has the regional hospital, 30-45 minutes from most spots. Camps run rescue boats during operating hours; outside them, there is no cover.
logistics.bookingWindows: Kite camps in July-August: 2-3 months. Nida accommodation in high summer: 3-4 months. May and September: 2-3 weeks.
logistics.health: Standing depth is what makes Svencelė forgiving, and it is also what makes a bad crash different: injuries here come from hitting a hard sand bottom, not from drowning. Helmet and impact vest are sensible, not optional, for anyone jumping.
logistics.gettingThere: A car makes the week: the two shores are separated by a ferry and an hour of driving, and the ability to chase wind between them is what turns four good days into six.

other.label: The Baltic has no meaningful tide
other.text: Water level here is a **wind-driven** variable: sustained westerlies raise the lagoon, easterlies drain it, and the difference over a week can be substantial in a bay this shallow. Ask the camp what the level is doing before assuming yesterday's depth.

other.label: Protected landscape
other.text: The Curonian Spit is a UNESCO site with strict dune and habitat protection: designated launches only, no walking on the dunes off boardwalks, no fires, and seasonal restrictions in bird areas. Fines are real.

other.label: The border
other.text: The southern half of the spit is in Russia's Kaliningrad exclave. Do not ride, sail or drift south of the marked boundary, this is a hard international border on the water as well as the land.

other.label: Water quality
other.text: Late-summer cyanobacteria blooms occur in the warm shallow lagoon. Advisories are posted; take them seriously, particularly for children and dogs.

proTips: **Learn here.** Svencelė is one of the best beginner kite spots in Europe: standing depth over a large area, consistent side-shore thermal, warm water in summer, and prices roughly half of Tarifa or the Netherlands.
Ride the **afternoon thermal**, and use the mornings for a foil session, a lesson or the spit. The wind pattern in midsummer is predictable enough to plan the day around.
Base at Svencelė and take **two nights in Nida** rather than commuting daily. The ferry, the eco-fee and the spit's speed limits make a daily round trip a waste of wind.
Bring or hire a **wing** as well as a kite. On light thermal days, wing foiling gets you on the water when kites are sitting on the beach, and this lagoon is close to perfect for it.
The lagoon's shallow warm water means a **shorty in July** is enough. Do not overpack neoprene for the Baltic's reputation; this is not the North Sea.
Combine with **Trip 10** if you want a partner or family who does not ride to enjoy the same week, Nida, the dunes and the cycle path are twenty minutes from the launch.

raw.prevailing_wind: Southwest to west dominant, with reliable summer sea-breeze thermals building through the afternoon. Northeasterlies are offshore on the mainland shore and side-shore at Svencelė's spit
raw.wind_statistics: Spring and autumn deliver the strongest gradient wind; midsummer relies on the thermal, which typically fills in early afternoon and holds until evening
launch_spots: Preila and Nida on the lagoon side
Melnragė and Giruliai on the Baltic side near Klaipėda
raw.equipment_hubs: Svencelė is the centre, schools, storage, rescue boats and rental on site; Nida has smaller operations
raw.tidal_awareness: The Baltic is effectively **non-tidal**, the range is a few centimetres. Water level is driven by wind instead: a sustained westerly pushes water into the lagoon and raises it, a strong easterly drains it and can leave the shallows unrideable. Plan by wind history, not by a tide table
raw.water_temp_c: 14-17 in May, 20-24 in July-August in the shallow lagoon, 15-18 in late September
raw.wetsuit_guidance: Shorty or 3/2 in midsummer; 4/3 in May and late September; the lagoon is far warmer than the open Baltic
